resonator.card_en: A device or structure that amplifies signals at specific frequencies, here made of layered material to enhance axion-to-photon conversion.

picosecond.card_en: A unit of time equal to one trillionth of a second.

aliases.name: trillionths_of_a_second
aliases.line: A unit of time equal to 10^-12 seconds, also known as a picosecond.

precision.card_en: The closeness of agreement between repeated measurements of the same quantity, indicating the repeatability of a sensor.

aliases.name: precision_measurement
aliases.line: The act of measuring a quantity with high accuracy and repeatability.

background.card_en: Unwanted signal from sources other than the target, contributing to measurement noise.

aliases.name: background_noise
aliases.line: Unwanted signals that obscure the measurement of a desired physical process.

quantum_effects.card_en: Phenomena arising from the quantum nature of fields, influencing macroscopic systems.

absorption.card_en: The process by which a system takes in energy from incoming waves or particles.

aliases.name: heat_absorption
aliases.line: The process by which a material takes in thermal energy.

aliases.name: absorbed_energy
aliases.line: The amount of energy transferred from an external wave to a material system.

aliases.name: radiation_absorption
aliases.line: The process by which a material takes up energy from electromagnetic radiation, often measured as a function of frequency.

astronomical_unit.card_en: A unit of length equal to the average distance between the Earth and the Sun, used for distances within planetary systems.

sky_survey.card_en: A sky survey is a systematic mapping of the sky to catalog astronomical objects and phenomena.

aliases.name: sky_surveys
aliases.line: Systematic observations of the sky to map galaxy distribution and lensing effects for cosmological studies.

aliases.name: space_survey
aliases.line: A systematic observation of a large portion of the sky to catalog celestial objects.

femtosecond.card_en: A unit of time equal to one quadrillionth of a second, used to measure ultrafast processes.

aliases.name: attosecond
aliases.line: A unit of time equal to one quintillionth of a second, used for ultra-fast processes.

conductivity.card_en: Ability of a material to conduct electric current, here combined with magnetism.

aliases.name: electrical_conductivity
aliases.line: The ability of a material to conduct electric current.

aliases.name: electron_conductivity
aliases.line: The ability of a material to conduct electric current via the movement of electrons.

electrode.card_en: A conductor through which current enters or leaves a battery.

ionization.card_en: The process of removing particles from an atom or molecule, here applied to the stripping of dark matter particles from the cloud.

disorder.card_en: A state lacking regular pattern or predictability in the arrangement of parts.

annihilation.card_en: The process where a particle and its antiparticle collide and convert their mass into energy.

aliases.name: pair_annihilation
aliases.line: The process where a particle and its antiparticle collide and convert their mass into radiation.

nanosecond.card_en: A unit of time equal to one billionth of a second, used to measure extremely short durations.

aliases.name: billionth_of_a_second
aliases.line: A unit of time equal to one nanosecond, used to measure ultrafast processes.

ground_state.card_en: The lowest energy state of a quantum system, from which excitations are measured.

aliases.name: ground_state_energy
aliases.line: The lowest possible energy of a quantum system, such as a nucleus.

excited_state.card_en: A higher-energy state of an atom or molecule, often leading to emission of light upon relaxation.

aliases.name: excited_atoms
aliases.line: Atoms in a higher energy state that can release energy by emitting photons.

aliases.name: excited_electron
aliases.line: An electron in a higher energy state than its ground state, whose relaxation can emit light.

compact_object.card_en: A dense astronomical object such as a white dwarf, neutron star, or black hole.

aliases.name: compact_star
aliases.line: A dense stellar remnant such as a white dwarf, neutron star, or black hole.

aliases.name: compact_astrophysical_object
aliases.line: A dense celestial body such as a neutron star or white dwarf, with strong gravitational effects.

matter_antimatter_asymmetry.card_en: The observed imbalance between matter and antimatter in the universe, explaining why matter survived.

decibel.card_en: A logarithmic unit used to express the ratio of two values, often power or intensity.

coherence.card_en: A property of waves where their phases are correlated, allowing for constructive interference.

aliases.name: wave_coherence
aliases.line: The property of waves maintaining a constant phase relationship, enabling interference effects.

amplitude.card_en: The maximum extent of a vibration or oscillation, measured from its equilibrium.

aliases.name: oscillation_amplitude
aliases.line: The maximum extent of a vibration or oscillation from its equilibrium position.

aliases.name: wave_amplitude
aliases.line: The maximum extent of a wave's oscillation, often related to its energy or intensity.

ion.card_en: An atom or molecule with a net electric charge due to loss or gain of electrons, used as qubits here.

aliases.name: iron_ion
aliases.line: An atom of iron that has lost or gained electrons, giving it a net electric charge.

aliases.name: oxygen_ion
aliases.line: An atom of oxygen that has lost or gained electrons, giving it a net electric charge.

aliases.name: ions
aliases.line: Atoms or molecules that have a net electric charge due to the loss or gain of electrons.

aliases.name: metal_ion
aliases.line: An atom of a metal that has lost or gained electrons, carrying a net electric charge.

aliases.name: cobalt_ion
aliases.line: A cobalt atom that has lost or gained electrons, carrying a net electric charge.

absorption_line.card_en: A dark line in a spectrum caused by the absorption of specific wavelengths of light by atoms or ions in a gas.

aliases.name: absorption_spectrum
aliases.line: The pattern of dark lines in a spectrum caused by atoms absorbing specific wavelengths of light.

aliases.name: absorption_lines
aliases.line: Dark lines in a spectrum where gas absorbs light at specific frequencies, revealing its composition and motion.

aliases.name: helium_absorption_line
aliases.line: A spectral feature caused by helium atoms absorbing light at a specific wavelength.

aliases.name: absorption_feature
aliases.line: An absorption feature is a dark line or band in a spectrum caused by gas absorbing specific wavelengths.

positron.card_en: The antimatter counterpart of the electron, predicted by Dirac and described as an electron moving backward in time.

virgo.card_en: A gravitational-wave detector in Europe, operating as an interferometer alongside LIGO.

gluon.card_en: The force carrier that binds quarks together, generating most of the proton's mass.

fine_tuning.card_en: The requirement that initial conditions or parameters must be precisely set for a theory to match observations.

electric_charge.card_en: A fundamental property of matter that causes it to experience a force in an electromagnetic field.

supercomputer.card_en: A high-performance computing system used for complex simulations and calculations.

energy_loss.card_en: The reduction of a particle's energy as it passes through matter.

aliases.name: energy_attenuation
aliases.line: The reduction of particle energy as it passes through absorbing material.

evaporation.card_en: The transition of a substance from a liquid or solid state to a gas.

aliases.name: vaporization
aliases.line: The phase transition of a substance from liquid to gas, here referring to ice turning into vapor.

gigapascal.card_en: A unit of pressure equal to one billion pascals, commonly used in high-pressure physics.

aliases.name: megapascal
aliases.line: A unit of pressure or stress equal to one million pascals, commonly used in materials science.

aliases.name: terapascal
aliases.line: A unit of pressure equal to one trillion pascals, used for extreme compression studies.

chemical_composition.card_en: The identity and relative amounts of substances making up a material or object.

aliases.name: composition
aliases.line: The makeup of a substance or object in terms of its constituent parts.

aliases.name: molecular_composition
aliases.line: The relative abundances of different molecules in a gas or region.

kiloelectronvolt.card_en: A unit of energy equal to one thousand electronvolts, used in atomic and nuclear physics.

aliases.name: millielectronvolt
aliases.line: A unit of energy equal to one thousandth of an electronvolt, used for tiny particle masses.

aliases.name: kilo_electronvolt
aliases.line: A unit of energy equal to one thousand electronvolts, used for nuclear-scale measurements.

energy_gap.card_en: The minimum energy required to excite a system from its ground state.

charged_particles.card_en: Particles carrying electric charge, whose collisions were simulated in this experiment.

new_physics.card_en: Phenomena or particles beyond the Standard Model of particle physics, potentially revealing extra dimensions or new fields.

galactic_center.card_en: The central region of a galaxy, often dense with stars and gas.

aliases.name: galactic_core
aliases.line: The central region of a galaxy, often containing a dense concentration of stars and possibly a supermassive black hole.

aliases.name: galaxy_center
aliases.line: The central region of a galaxy, often hosting a supermassive black hole.

thermal_radiation.card_en: Electromagnetic radiation emitted by a body due to its temperature, including the vacuum radiation seen by accelerating observers.

aliases.name: thermal_emission
aliases.line: Electromagnetic radiation emitted by an object due to its temperature.

aliases.name: thermal_vacuum_radiation
aliases.line: Radiation that appears in a vacuum due to acceleration or spacetime curvature, making the vacuum appear to have a temperature.

teraelectronvolt.card_en: A unit of energy equal to one trillion electronvolts, used for high-energy particles.

aliases.name: petaelectronvolt
aliases.line: A unit of energy equal to one quadrillion electronvolts, used for extremely high-energy particles.

aliases.name: peta_electronvolt
aliases.line: A unit of energy equal to one quadrillion electronvolts, used for extremely high-energy particles.

aliases.name: tera_electronvolt
aliases.line: A unit of energy equal to one trillion electronvolts, used for high-energy particles and photons.

gas_giant.card_en: A large planet composed mostly of gases, such as hydrogen and helium, like Jupiter or Saturn.

aliases.name: giant_planet
aliases.line: A massive planet primarily composed of hydrogen and helium, such as Jupiter.

aliases.name: giant_planets
aliases.line: Large planets primarily composed of hydrogen and helium, such as Jupiter and Saturn.

millikelvin.card_en: A unit of temperature equal to one thousandth of a kelvin, used for ultra-cold environments.

aliases.name: nanokelvin
aliases.line: A unit of temperature equal to one billionth of a kelvin, used in ultracold experiments.

aliases.name: picokelvin
aliases.line: A unit of temperature equal to one trillionth of a kelvin, used for ultra-cold matter.

magnetic_field_sensor.card_en: A device or system that detects the presence and strength of magnetic fields.

aliases.name: magnetic_sensor
aliases.line: A device that measures magnetic fields, with sensitivity enhanced by quantum entanglement.

schwarzschild_black_hole.card_en: The simplest black hole solution, with no charge or rotation, described by Karl Schwarzschild.

space_weather.card_en: Conditions in space driven by solar activity that can affect Earth's environment and technology.

correlation.card_en: A statistical relationship between two or more variables, here referring to entangled particle states.

aliases.name: correlations
aliases.line: Statistical relationships between two or more variables indicating how they vary together.

waveguide.card_en: A structure that guides electromagnetic waves, here used to direct photons through the chip.

aliases.name: open_waveguide
aliases.line: A structure that guides electromagnetic waves, here used to collect emitted photons from a qubit.

aliases.name: waveguide_cable
aliases.line: A structure that guides electromagnetic waves, here used to transmit radio signals along a defined path.

luminosity.card_en: The total amount of energy a star emits per unit time.

aliases.name: solar_luminosity
aliases.line: The total amount of energy emitted by the Sun per unit time.

aliases.name: total_luminosity
aliases.line: The total amount of energy emitted by a star per unit time across all wavelengths.

aliases.name: neutrino_luminosity
aliases.line: The total amount of neutrino energy emitted by an object per unit time.

red_giant.card_en: A large, cool, luminous star in a late stage of stellar evolution.

aliases.name: red_supergiant
aliases.line: A very large, bright, cool star in a late stage of evolution, hundreds of times wider than the Sun.

core_collapse.card_en: The gravitational collapse of the iron core of a massive star, triggering a supernova explosion.

aliases.name: stellar_collapse
aliases.line: The gravitational collapse of a massive star's core at the end of its life.

aliases.name: stellar_core_collapse
aliases.line: The gravitational collapse of the central region of a massive star at the end of its life.

aliases.name: core_collapse_supernovae
aliases.line: Explosive deaths of massive stars when their cores collapse under gravity, producing gravitational waves and neutrinos.

rotation.card_en: A motion of an object around an axis, described by a set of transformations.

molecular_cloud.card_en: A collection of molecules held together, often in a trap, used for cooling and precision experiments.

aliases.name: atom_cloud
aliases.line: A collection of atoms, often cooled and trapped, used in experiments to study quantum phenomena.

brightness.card_en: The amount of light emitted or reflected by an object, often measured in magnitudes or flux.

aliases.name: emission_brightness
aliases.line: The intensity of light emitted by a source, often measured in relative units.

frequency_shift.card_en: A change in the frequency of a wave, often due to motion or modulation.

aliases.name: frequency_change
aliases.line: The rate at which the frequency of a signal, such as a gravitational wave, changes over time.

thermodynamics.card_en: The branch of physics dealing with heat, work, and energy transfer in physical systems.

aliases.name: classical_thermodynamics
aliases.line: The branch of physics dealing with heat, work, and energy in macroscopic systems.

aliases.name: thermodynamic
aliases.line: Relating to the relationships between heat, work, temperature, and energy in a system.

elasticity.card_en: The property of a material to deform under stress and return to its original shape when the stress is removed.

aliases.name: elastic_solid
aliases.line: A material that returns to its original shape after applied stress is removed.

aliases.name: elastic_deformation
aliases.line: Temporary deformation of a material that is fully recoverable when the applied stress is removed.

aliases.name: elastic_material
aliases.line: A material that returns to its original shape after the deforming force is removed.

solar_cell.card_en: A device that converts light energy directly into electrical energy via the photovoltaic effect.

aliases.name: solar_panel
aliases.line: A device that converts light into electricity, a potential application of superabsorption.

aliases.name: organic_solar_cell
aliases.line: A carbon-based photovoltaic device that converts light to electricity, benefiting from efficient dark states.

quantum_corrections.card_en: Modifications to classical physics equations that account for quantum mechanical effects.

aliases.name: quantum_correction
aliases.line: A modification to classical predictions arising from quantum fluctuations or uncertainties.

gravitational_wave_background.card_en: A stochastic signal of gravitational waves from many sources, potentially imprinted by dark matter dynamics.

aliases.name: stochastic_gravitational_wave_background
aliases.line: A random gravitational-wave signal from many unresolved sources, studied here in the microhertz frequency range.

aliases.name: background_gravitational_waves
aliases.line: A stochastic signal of gravitational waves from many unresolved sources, forming a cosmic background.

quasinormal_modes.card_en: The characteristic damped oscillations of a perturbed black hole or other compact object, revealing its properties.

aliases.name: quasinormal_mode
aliases.line: Characteristic damped oscillations of a black hole after a perturbation, with frequencies and damping times set by its properties.

aliases.name: quasi_normal_mode
aliases.line: The characteristic oscillations of a perturbed black hole as it returns to equilibrium.

aliases.name: quasinormal_frequencies
aliases.line: Complex frequencies characterizing the damped oscillations of a black hole after perturbation.

energy_dissipation.card_en: The process by which energy is lost or transformed, during which entanglement can emerge here.

aliases.name: dissipation
aliases.line: The process by which energy is lost from a system, often as heat, leading to decay.

quantum_materials.card_en: Materials where quantum mechanical effects are essential to their properties, such as high-temperature superconductors and topological insulators.

aliases.name: quantum_material
aliases.line: A material whose properties are strongly influenced by quantum mechanical effects, such as superconductivity or magnetic order.

charge.card_en: An intrinsic property of atomic nuclei that influences their acceleration and detection.

quantum_internet.card_en: A future network that uses quantum states, such as photons, to transmit information securely.

weak_interaction.card_en: One of the four fundamental forces, responsible for radioactive decay and particle transformations.

alloy.card_en: A metallic substance made by mixing and melting two or more elements, at least one of which is a metal.

aliases.name: alloying
aliases.line: The process of combining a metal with another element to form an alloy.

charge_carrier.card_en: A particle that carries electric charge in a current, here protons instead of electrons.

aliases.name: charge_carriers
aliases.line: Particles such as electrons or holes that carry electric charge in a material.

radiation_dose.card_en: The amount of radiation energy absorbed by tissue, a key parameter in treatment planning.

aliases.name: dose
aliases.line: The amount of radiation energy absorbed per unit mass of a material or tissue.

aliases.name: radiation_dose_calculation
aliases.line: The process of determining the amount of radiation to be delivered to a patient during therapy.

amplification.card_en: The process of increasing the magnitude of a signal or effect.

aliases.name: signal_amplification
aliases.line: The process of increasing the strength of a signal, here applied to gravitational wave detection.

aliases.name: light_amplification
aliases.line: The process of increasing the intensity of light through repeated reflections.

aliases.name: power_amplification
aliases.line: Increasing the peak power output of a system relative to its average or steady-state power.

vibration.card_en: Oscillatory motion of a physical system about an equilibrium position.

aliases.name: atomic_vibration
aliases.line: The oscillation of atoms around their equilibrium positions in a material.

aliases.name: mechanical_vibration
aliases.line: Oscillation of a physical system around an equilibrium position, such as a tuning fork or nanotube.

ion_trap.card_en: A device that uses electric fields to confine charged particles in a vacuum.

sigma.card_en: A unit of statistical significance, where higher sigma indicates stronger evidence.

x_ray_emission.card_en: High-energy electromagnetic radiation emitted by hot astrophysical plasmas and accreting objects.

aliases.name: high_energy_emission
aliases.line: Electromagnetic radiation at high energies, such as X-rays or gamma rays.

transition_temperature.card_en: The temperature below which a material becomes superconducting.

aliases.name: superconducting_transition_temperature
aliases.line: The temperature below which a material becomes superconducting, tunable in alloys for detector design.

aliases.name: superconducting_transition
aliases.line: The change of a material's state to a superconducting phase at a characteristic critical temperature.

radio_signal.card_en: Electromagnetic radiation in the radio frequency range, used for communication and astronomical observation.

aliases.name: radio_frequency
aliases.line: The range of electromagnetic frequencies used for radio communication and astronomy.

aliases.name: radio_frequency_signal
aliases.line: An electromagnetic signal in the radio frequency range, used for controlling or reading out qubits.

hole.card_en: The absence of an electron in a crystal lattice, acting as a positive charge carrier.

instability.card_en: A condition where small disturbances grow over time, leading to a new state.

tess.card_en: The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, a space telescope that detects exoplanets and other transiting objects via photometry.

reflection.card_en: The change in direction of a wave when it bounces off a surface or boundary.

aliases.name: wave_reflection
aliases.line: The bouncing back of a wave when it encounters a boundary or obstacle.

aliases.name: reflect
aliases.line: To bounce a wave off a surface, changing its direction.

aliases.name: signal_reflection
aliases.line: The change in direction of a wavefront when it encounters a surface, returning into the medium it came from.

massive_star.card_en: A star with a mass significantly greater than the Sun's, which typically ends its life in a supernova explosion.

aliases.name: supermassive_star
aliases.line: A very massive star, often hundreds of thousands of solar masses, that lives briefly and ends in collapse.

aliases.name: massive_stars
aliases.line: Stars with masses significantly greater than the Sun, which are hot, luminous, and short-lived.

model.card_en: A simplified mathematical or conceptual representation of a physical system.

aliases.name: physical_model
aliases.line: A mathematical representation of a system based on physical laws and principles.

sound_wave.card_en: A mechanical pressure wave that propagates through a medium, such as air or tissue.

aliases.name: sound_waves
aliases.line: A mechanical wave of pressure and displacement that propagates through a medium like air or a solid.

aliases.name: sound
aliases.line: A mechanical wave that propagates through a medium as a pressure or displacement disturbance.

aliases.name: pressure_wave
aliases.line: A wave of pressure that travels through a medium, such as blood in arteries.

speed_of_sound.card_en: The speed at which sound waves propagate through a medium.

aliases.name: sound_speed
aliases.line: The speed at which pressure waves travel through a medium, which affects the stiffness and maximum mass of a neutron star.

aliases.name: wave_speed
aliases.line: The velocity at which a wave of cell density propagates through a medium.

antiferromagnet.card_en: A material where neighboring atomic magnetic moments point in opposite directions, resulting in no net magnetization.

aliases.name: antiferromagnetism
aliases.line: A type of magnetic order where neighboring magnetic moments align in opposite directions.

diamond.card_en: A solid form of carbon with a crystal structure.

type_ia_supernova.card_en: A type of supernova used as a standard candle for measuring cosmic distances.

critical_point.card_en: The point at which a continuous phase transition occurs and the energy gap vanishes.

dust.card_en: Small solid particles in space, a key component of protoplanetary disks.

pion.card_en: A type of meson, a subatomic particle made of quarks.

einstein_telescope.card_en: A proposed third-generation ground-based gravitational wave detector with high sensitivity.

efficiency.card_en: The ratio of useful work output to total energy input in a thermodynamic process.

aliases.name: thermodynamic_efficiency
aliases.line: A measure of how effectively energy input is converted into useful work in a system.

probability.card_en: A measure of the likelihood that a particular quantum interaction or event occurs.

aliases.name: probabilities
aliases.line: Numerical measures of the likelihood of a particular outcome occurring in a physical process.

aliases.name: quantum_probability
aliases.line: The probability of an event as determined by quantum mechanical principles.

two_dimensional_material.card_en: A material consisting of a single layer of atoms, exhibiting distinct physical properties.

aliases.name: 2d_material
aliases.line: A material consisting of a single layer of atoms or molecules, exhibiting unique properties.

aliases.name: 2d_materials
aliases.line: Layers of material one atom thick with unique properties, often compared to a sheet of paper.

amino_acid.card_en: Organic molecules that serve as the building blocks of proteins.

aliases.name: amino_acids
aliases.line: Organic molecules that serve as the building blocks of proteins, essential for life.

x_ray_telescope.card_en: A telescope designed to detect and image X-ray radiation from astronomical sources.

aliases.name: xray_telescope
aliases.line: A telescope designed to detect X-ray emissions from high-energy cosmic objects like supernova remnants.

aliases.name: x_ray_observatory
aliases.line: A telescope designed to detect X-ray emissions from high-energy cosmic phenomena.

diagnosis.card_en: The process of identifying a disease or condition based on its signs and symptoms.

aliases.name: diagnostics
aliases.line: The process of identifying a disease or condition from its signs and symptoms.

aliases.name: diagnostic
aliases.line: A procedure or test used to identify a disease or condition based on its signs and symptoms.

aliases.name: disease_detection
aliases.line: The identification of a disease or condition through diagnostic imaging.

aliases.name: psychological_diagnosis
aliases.line: The process of identifying a mental condition based on symptoms or behavioral metrics.

coupling.card_en: The interaction strength between quantum systems, here tunable via a magnetic field to control energy flow.

methane.card_en: A molecule in brown dwarf atmospheres whose light fluctuations indicate chemical activity.

microscope.card_en: An instrument used to see objects too small for the naked eye, requiring stability.

aliases.name: microscopic
aliases.line: Describing objects or structures too small to be seen with the naked eye, requiring a microscope.

nitrogen_vacancy_center.group: diamond magnetometry · nv center sensing · diamond nv center
nitrogen_vacancy_center.card_en: A crystal lattice defect in diamond where a nitrogen atom replaces carbon adjacent to a vacancy, hosting a spin.

aliases.name: nitrogen_vacancy
aliases.line: A defect in diamond where a nitrogen atom replaces carbon and a neighboring carbon is missing, acting as a magnet.

optical_cavity.card_en: A setup of mirrors that traps light, allowing it to bounce and amplify signals.

aliases.name: mirror_cavity
aliases.line: An optical setup with two or more mirrors that traps light, enhancing its interaction with matter inside.

scanning_tunneling_microscope.card_en: A microscope that images surfaces at the atomic scale by measuring tunneling current between a sharp tip and the sample.

aliases.name: scanning_tunneling_microscopy
aliases.line: A technique using a sharp tip to image surfaces at the atomic scale by measuring tunneling current.

aliases.name: tunneling_microscope
aliases.line: A microscope that uses quantum tunneling to image and manipulate individual atoms.

aliases.name: tunneling_microscopy
aliases.line: A microscopy technique that images surfaces at the atomic scale by measuring electron tunneling current.

flux.card_en: The rate of flow of a quantity, such as particles or energy, through a unit area.

aliases.name: particle_flux
aliases.line: The rate at which particles arrive per unit area and time, often as a function of energy.

aliases.name: electron_flux
aliases.line: The rate of flow of electrons per unit area per unit time, measured as a function of energy.

aliases.name: light_flux
aliases.line: The rate of flow of light energy through a unit area, a measure of an object's apparent brightness.

aliases.name: mass_flux
aliases.line: The rate of mass flow through a unit area per unit time.

aliases.name: flux_distribution
aliases.line: The distribution of the rate of energy flow per unit area from observed bursts.

planetary_system.card_en: A set of planets and other bodies orbiting a star.

gas_cloud.card_en: A concentration of gas in space, often detected via absorption lines in quasar spectra.

momentum.card_en: The product of mass and velocity, a measure of motion that can be lost or gained.

chemical_reaction.card_en: A process that involves rearrangement of the molecular or ionic structure of a substance.

quantum_coherence.card_en: The property of a quantum system where its parts maintain a fixed phase relationship, enabling interference effects.

aliases.name: quantum_phase_coherence
aliases.line: The property of a quantum system where its wavefunction maintains a fixed phase relationship over time and space.

fusion_reactor.card_en: A device that generates energy by fusing atomic nuclei, typically hydrogen isotopes, at extremely high temperatures.

aliases.name: fusion_reactors
aliases.line: Devices designed to harness energy from nuclear fusion reactions.

pulsar_timing_array.card_en: A network of pulsars used to detect gravitational waves by monitoring correlated timing variations.

aliases.name: pulsar_timing
aliases.line: Technique monitoring pulsar pulse arrival times to detect gravitational waves or other disturbances.

aliases.name: pulsar_timing_arrays
aliases.line: Networks of radio telescopes that monitor pulsar pulse arrival times to detect gravitational waves.

galactic_disk.card_en: The flattened, rotating region of a spiral galaxy where most of its gas and stars reside.

aliases.name: stellar_disk
aliases.line: The flattened, rotating region of a spiral galaxy where most of its stars reside.

aliases.name: milky_way_disk
aliases.line: The flattened, rotating plane of the Milky Way galaxy where most stars reside.

aliases.name: galaxy_disk
aliases.line: The flattened, rotating region of a galaxy containing most of its stars and gas.

silicon.card_en: A chemical element with symbol Si, a common component of cosmic dust.

electron_beam.card_en: A stream of electrons used as a projectile in scattering experiments.

domain_wall.card_en: A boundary between regions of different magnetization in a magnetic material.

aliases.name: magnetic_domain_wall
aliases.line: A narrow transition region in a magnet where the magnetization direction gradually rotates between areas of uniform magnetization.

celsius.card_en: A unit of temperature where water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees.

aliases.name: degree_celsius
aliases.line: A unit of temperature on the Celsius scale, where 0°C is the freezing point of water.

cross_section.card_en: A measure of the probability of a specific nuclear reaction occurring, expressed as an effective area.

aliases.name: reaction_cross_section
aliases.line: A measure of the probability of a nuclear reaction occurring.

radiation_therapy.card_en: Medical treatment using ionizing radiation to kill cancer cells or shrink tumors.

aliases.name: radiotherapy
aliases.line: Medical treatment using radiation to damage or kill cancer cells.

threshold.card_en: A minimum value of brightness or duration above which a signal is considered detectable.

aliases.name: detection_threshold
aliases.line: The minimum brightness or signal level required for an object to be detected in an observation.

first_order_phase_transition.card_en: A discontinuous transition between states of matter or systems, occurring abruptly at a specific threshold.

aliases.name: first_order_transition
aliases.line: A phase transition involving latent heat, characterized by a discontinuity in order parameters.

temperature_map.card_en: A map showing the distribution of temperature, often of the cosmic microwave background.

aliases.name: thermal_map
aliases.line: A visual representation of temperature distribution across a surface, often captured by imaging techniques.

photomultiplier_tube.card_en: A vacuum tube that converts light flashes into amplified electrical signals.

aliases.name: photomultiplier
aliases.line: A vacuum tube device that amplifies faint light signals into measurable electrical pulses.

lubricant.card_en: A substance that reduces friction between surfaces, here the water film under ice.

aliases.name: lubrication
aliases.line: Use of a substance to reduce friction between surfaces in contact.

left_ventricle.card_en: The main pumping chamber of the heart that pushes oxygenated blood to the body.

aliases.name: ventricle

aliases.name: right_ventricle

xray_polarization.card_en: The property of X-ray waves oscillating in a preferred direction, used to probe magnetic field structures.

aliases.name: x_ray_polarization

millimeter_emission.card_en: Electromagnetic radiation emitted at millimeter wavelengths, often from hot gas around compact objects.

aliases.name: submillimeter_emission

bottom_quark.card_en: A heavy quark, also called beauty quark, about four times heavier than a proton.

aliases.name: beauty_quark
aliases.line: A heavy quark, also known as the bottom quark, that is a constituent of certain hadrons.

microbial_community.card_en: A collection of microorganisms living together in a shared environment, such as the gut, ocean, or soil.

aliases.name: microbial_population

aliases.name: microbiome
aliases.line: The community of microorganisms, such as bacteria, living in a particular environment like the gut or skin.

fracture.card_en: The separation of a material into pieces under stress, often initiated by crack propagation.

aliases.name: crack
aliases.line: A fracture in a material that can propagate under stress, often leading to failure.

atlas_experiment.card_en: A particle detector at the Large Hadron Collider used to study high-energy proton collisions.

aliases.name: cms_experiment

rigidity.card_en: A particle's energy divided by its charge, determining its bending in a magnetic field.

aliases.name: magnetic_rigidity

electron_charge.card_en: The fundamental unit of electric charge carried by a single electron.

aliases.name: elementary_charge
aliases.line: The fundamental unit of electric charge carried by a single electron or proton.

magnetic_susceptibility.card_en: A dimensionless quantity indicating how much a material becomes magnetized in an applied magnetic field.

aliases.name: susceptibility
aliases.line: A measure of how readily a material responds to an applied magnetic field.

ultra_fast_outflow.card_en: A powerful wind of ionized gas from an active galactic nucleus moving at a significant fraction of the speed of light.

aliases.name: ultrafast_outflow

acoustic_oscillations.card_en: Sound waves in the early universe that left imprints on the distribution of galaxies.

aliases.name: sound_waves_in_early_universe

aliases.name: sound_waves_in_early_plasma

pipeline.card_en: A sequence of data processing steps used to convert raw observations into scientific products.

aliases.name: signal_processing_pipeline

aliases.name: data_pipeline
aliases.line: A series of automated data processing steps to transform raw data into usable outputs.

dark_matter_subhalo.card_en: A small, self-bound clump of dark matter orbiting within a larger dark matter halo.

aliases.name: dark_subhalo

aliases.name: subhalo

biology.card_en: The scientific study of life and living organisms.

aliases.name: ecology

schrodinger_cat_state.card_en: A quantum superposition of a macroscopic object in two distinct states, used to test quantum mechanics at large scales.

cosmological_data.card_en: Observational data from astronomical surveys used to study the universe's large-scale properties and evolution.

aliases.name: cosmological_data_analysis

gwtc.card_en: The Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, a public catalog of gravitational-wave events from LIGO and Virgo.

aliases.name: gwtc_4_catalog

frequency_standard.card_en: A device that provides a precise, stable frequency reference for timekeeping and measurements.

aliases.name: optical_frequency_standard

aliases.name: mechanical_frequency_standard
aliases.line: A device that provides a stable, precise frequency reference based on mechanical vibrations.

metal_poor.card_en: A star with a low abundance of elements heavier than helium in its atmosphere.

aliases.name: metal_poor_galaxy

blackbody.card_en: A blackbody is an idealized object that absorbs all radiation and emits a characteristic spectrum depending only on its temperature.

aliases.name: black_body
aliases.line: An idealized physical body that absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation and emits thermal radiation.

aliases.name: blackbody_emission
aliases.line: Thermal radiation emitted by an idealized object that absorbs all incident radiation.

molecular_interaction.card_en: Forces between molecules that influence their arrangement and behavior on a surface.

aliases.name: mutual_interactions

aliases.name: molecular_interactions
aliases.line: The forces and effects that occur between molecules.

positive_feedback_loop.card_en: A process where an effect amplifies its own cause, leading to a self-sustaining state.

aliases.name: positive_feedback
aliases.line: A process where an effect amplifies its own cause, leading to accelerated growth or change.

spectral_energy_distribution.card_en: The distribution of electromagnetic radiation emitted by an object as a function of wavelength or frequency.

aliases.name: spectral_shape

dense_clump.card_en: A dense knot of gas and dust within a molecular cloud that can become the site of star formation.

aliases.name: massive_clump

aliases.name: gas_clump
aliases.line: A dense, localized concentration of gas within a molecular cloud that may collapse to form a star.

scalable.card_en: Scalable refers to the ability of a system to expand in size or capacity without performance loss.

aliases.name: scalability
aliases.line: The ability of a system to increase in size or capacity without a loss in performance or control.

topological_transition.card_en: A change in the topological properties of a physical system, often marked by a phase transition.

reference_frame.card_en: A coordinate system used to measure positions and motions, which can affect observed physical quantities.

aliases.name: frame_of_reference
aliases.line: A coordinate system used to measure physical quantities, whose choice can affect calculations.

automated_analysis.card_en: The use of computer algorithms to process and interpret data without manual intervention.

aliases.name: automated_processing
aliases.line: The use of computer algorithms to perform data processing tasks without human intervention.

aliases.name: machine_analysis
aliases.line: The use of computer algorithms to automatically analyze data, often without explicit physical knowledge.

photoelectron.card_en: An electron emitted from a material when it absorbs a photon.

nuclear_fragment.card_en: A piece of a nucleus produced when a heavy nucleus breaks apart in a collision.

permanent_magnet.card_en: A material that retains its magnetic properties after an external magnetic field is removed.

aliases.name: residual_magnetic_moment
aliases.line: The permanent magnetic moment remaining in a material after an external field is removed.

anti_reflective_coating.card_en: A thin film applied to optical surfaces to reduce reflection and glare.

aliases.line: A surface treatment that reduces reflection and increases transmission of light through an optical element.

aliases.name: antireflection_coating
aliases.line: A coating applied to an optical surface to reduce reflection and increase transmission of light.

lattice_defect.card_en: An imperfection in the regular periodic arrangement of atoms in a crystal.

aliases.name: crystal_imperfection

aliases.name: crystal_defects

helium_burning.card_en: The nuclear fusion of helium into heavier elements in a star's core.

aliases.name: helium_core_burning

aliases.name: helium_shell_burning

optical_distortion.card_en: Aberration or bending of light as it passes through a lens, degrading image or beam quality.

blood_test.card_en: A laboratory analysis of a blood sample used to assess health conditions or disease markers.

parallel_processing.card_en: A computation method where multiple operations are executed simultaneously.

aliases.name: parallelization
aliases.line: Performing multiple operations simultaneously to increase throughput or efficiency.

strength.card_en: The ability of a material to withstand applied force without deformation or failure.

aliases.name: metal_strength

stochastic_inflation.card_en: A framework that treats the inflaton field's quantum fluctuations as a stochastic process to model inflation.

quantum_light.card_en: Light exhibiting non-classical statistical properties, such as photon bunching.

photon_counting.card_en: A technique to detect and count individual photons, enabling signal extraction from bright backgrounds.

aliases.name: photon_counter
aliases.line: A device that detects and counts individual photons.

multi_field_inflation.card_en: Inflation driven by more than one scalar field, leading to distinct observational signatures.

hills_mechanism.card_en: The Hills mechanism is a process where a binary star system is disrupted by a black hole, capturing one star into a tight orbit.

information_spread.card_en: The process by which information propagates through a quantum system, often quantified by entanglement growth.

aliases.name: information_spreading
aliases.line: The process by which information propagates through a quantum system, often limited by the speed of light.

spectral_fitting.card_en: The model fits the observed spectrum from X-rays to highest energies.

error_suppression.card_en: Techniques used to reduce the impact of errors in quantum computations or simulations.

superradiant_phase_transition.card_en: A phase transition where electrons and photons synchronize, forming a collective state of matter and radiation.

fermionic_dark_matter.card_en: Dark matter composed of fermions, particles with half-integer spin, as opposed to bosonic candidates.

kinetic_simulation.card_en: A computer simulation that models the motion and interactions of individual particles in a plasma.

quantum_ising_model.card_en: A simplified quantum mechanical model of a magnet near a phase transition.

effective_number_of_neutrino_species.card_en: A measure of the energy density of light particles in the early universe, affected by gravitational waves.

noise_subtraction.card_en: An algorithm subtracts sensor noise from images of entangled photon pairs.

protein_language_model.card_en: A machine learning model trained on protein sequences to predict structures and design new proteins.

quantum_classical_boundary.card_en: The conceptual divide between quantum and classical physical behavior.

unconventional_superconductivity.card_en: Superconductivity that cannot be explained by the conventional BCS theory, often involving more complex pairing mechanisms.

active_learning.card_en: A machine learning approach where the algorithm selects the most informative data points to learn from, improving efficiency.

effective_spin.card_en: A measure of the combined spin of a black hole binary system, projected along the orbital axis.

domain_walls.card_en: Thin layers in space where the vacuum properties change abruptly, forming during a phase transition.

qubit_lifetime.group: qubit · three photon entanglement · quantum algorithm
qubit_lifetime.card_en: The duration a qubit retains its quantum state before decoherence, a key measure of performance.

aliases.name: quantum_state_lifetime
aliases.line: The duration a quantum state persists before decoherence, measured for the qubit in this experiment.

frequency_modulation.card_en: A technique where the frequency of a signal is varied smoothly over time to improve signal detection.

aliases.name: radiofrequency_modulation
aliases.line: The technique of varying a radiofrequency signal's properties to control or probe a system.

interaction_model.card_en: A theoretical framework describing how dark energy and dark matter exchange energy over time.

quantum_annealer.card_en: A machine that uses quantum effects to find the minimum energy state of a system.

aliases.name: superconducting_quantum_annealer
aliases.line: A machine that solves optimization problems by finding energy minima of a physical system.

supersymmetric_quantum_mechanics.card_en: A mathematical framework that relates complex quantum problems to simpler ones via supersymmetry transformations.

entropic_gravity.card_en: A theory proposing that gravity emerges from the statistical behavior of microscopic degrees of freedom.

optically_detected_magnetic_resonance.card_en: A technique that uses light to detect magnetic resonance signals from defects, used for quantum sensing.

cosmological_constant_problem.group: cosmological constant · dark energy · cosmic acceleration deceleration
cosmological_constant_problem.card_en: The discrepancy between the observed and predicted values of the cosmological constant.

electromagnetically_induced_transparency.card_en: A quantum interference effect that makes an opaque medium transparent to a probe beam when a second beam is applied.

fq_gravity.group: spacetime curvature · quantum bounce · quantum gravity effects
fq_gravity.card_en: A modified theory of gravity where gravity arises from spacetime non-metricity rather than curvature.

tes.card_en: Transition-edge sensor, a type of superconducting detector for measuring tiny energy changes.

triplet_superconductivity.card_en: A form of superconductivity where electron pairs have parallel spins, allowing supercurrents to flow through magnetic materials.

gravitational_instanton.card_en: A solution to Euclidean gravity equations, representing a rare field configuration in imaginary time used to calculate quantum probabilities.

inelastic_neutron_scattering.card_en: Probes phonon and magnon dispersions to reveal magnetoelastic coupling.

pump_probe_spectroscopy.card_en: Measures ultrafast dynamics by exciting with pump pulse and probing with delayed pulse.

monte_carlo_sampling.card_en: Stochastic method for estimating expectation values and thermal properties in quantum systems.

heralded_single_photon_generation.card_en: Produces triggered single photons via spontaneous parametric down-conversion or four-wave mixing.

newtonian_limit.group: Hawking area theorem · Birkhoff's theorem · equivalence principle
newtonian_limit.card_en: General relativity reduces to Newtonian gravity in weak-field, slow-motion approximation.

charge_qubit.card_en: Superconducting qubit whose two logical states are distinguished by the number of Cooper pairs.

group_theory.card_en: Symmetry analysis used to classify magnetic order and altermagnetic spin-splitting.

magneto_optical_kerr_effect.card_en: Measures magnetization via polarization rotation of reflected light.

cosmic_microwave_background_measurement.card_en: Observational technique mapping relic radiation to probe early universe conditions and parameters.

decoherence_free_subspace.card_en: Subspace of states immune to collective noise, used for robust quantum memory.

molecular_property_prediction.card_en: A task in cheminformatics where machine learning models predict properties of molecules from their structure.

airy_disk_constant.card_en: First zero of the Airy disk for a circular aperture

avogadro_constant.card_en: Number of constituent particles per mole

coulomb_constant.card_en: Electrostatic force constant in Coulomb's law

elementary_charge.card_en: Magnitude of the electric charge of a single electron or proton

gas_constant.card_en: Universal gas constant relating energy scale to temperature

magnetic_flux_quantum.card_en: Superconducting flux quantum, h/(2e), the fundamental unit of magnetic flux in a superconductor

planck_mass.card_en: Planck mass, the fundamental mass scale in quantum gravity

vacuum_permittivity.card_en: Permittivity of free space, a fundamental constant

wien_displacement_constant.card_en: Wien's displacement constant, relating peak wavelength to temperature

fine_structure_constant.card_en: Fine-structure constant, about 1/137 — the strength of the electromagnetic interaction, a pure number.

vacuum_permeability.card_en: Magnetic constant of vacuum, linking current to magnetic field.

faraday_constant.card_en: Charge of one mole of electrons.

rydberg_constant.card_en: Rydberg constant — sets the wavelengths of hydrogen spectral lines; the most precisely measured constant in physics.

bohr_radius.card_en: Bohr radius, the natural length scale of the hydrogen atom.

bohr_magneton.card_en: Bohr magneton, the natural unit of electron magnetic moment.

atomic_mass_constant.card_en: One twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

conductance_quantum.card_en: Conductance quantum 2e²/h — the step by which conductance changes in a quantum point contact.

von_klitzing_constant.card_en: Von Klitzing constant h/e² — the resistance plateau of the quantum Hall effect, now the resistance standard.

planck_length.card_en: Planck length, the scale at which spacetime itself is expected to need a quantum description.

planck_time.card_en: Planck time, light crossing one Planck length.

maximum_likelihood_estimation.card_en: Choosing the parameter values that make the observed data most probable under the model; the workhorse fit of experimental physics.

least_squares_fitting.card_en: Fitting by minimising the sum of squared residuals — the special case of maximum likelihood when errors are Gaussian and equal.

chi_squared_minimisation.card_en: Fitting by minimising chi-squared, the sum of squared residuals weighted by their uncertainties; its value at the minimum also measures goodness of fit.

weighted_mean.card_en: Combining measurements of different precision by weighting each by the inverse square of its uncertainty.

profile_likelihood.card_en: Handling nuisance parameters by maximising the likelihood over them at each value of the parameter of interest.

kernel_density_estimation.card_en: Estimating a smooth probability density from samples without assuming its functional form.

regularisation.card_en: Adding a penalty term to a fit to suppress wild solutions when the data underdetermine the model.

unfolding.card_en: Correcting a measured distribution for detector smearing to recover the true one — an ill-posed inversion that needs regularisation.

prior_distribution.card_en: What is assumed about a parameter before the data — the input of Bayesian analysis that most often decides its output.

metropolis_hastings_algorithm.card_en: The basic Markov chain rule: propose a step, accept it with a probability set by the ratio of posteriors.

nested_sampling.card_en: Sampling that computes the Bayesian evidence itself, not only the posterior; standard in gravitational-wave analysis.

hamiltonian_monte_carlo.card_en: Markov chain sampling that uses gradients of the posterior to take long, well-aimed steps in many dimensions.

gibbs_sampling.card_en: Sampling a multidimensional posterior one coordinate at a time from its conditional distributions.

credible_interval.card_en: The Bayesian interval containing a stated fraction of the posterior — the answer to 'where is the parameter', unlike a confidence interval.

bayesian_hierarchical_model.card_en: A model with parameters of parameters — the way to fit a population and its individual members at once.

bayesian_evidence.card_en: The probability of the data under a model with parameters integrated out; penalises complexity automatically.

null_hypothesis_testing.card_en: Asking how improbable the data would be if there were no effect — the frame in which discoveries are declared.

p_value.card_en: Probability of data at least as extreme as observed if the null hypothesis holds; not the probability that the hypothesis is true.

confidence_interval.card_en: The frequentist interval that would contain the true value in a stated fraction of repeated experiments.

likelihood_ratio_test.card_en: Comparing two nested models by the ratio of their maximum likelihoods; its distribution follows Wilks' theorem.

wilks_theorem.card_en: Result that twice the log likelihood ratio approaches a chi-squared distribution, which turns fits into significance.

kolmogorov_smirnov_test.card_en: Comparing two distributions by the largest gap between their cumulative curves, without binning.

anderson_darling_test.card_en: A distribution comparison weighted towards the tails, where the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test is weakest.

student_t_test.card_en: Comparing means of small samples when the variance itself is estimated from the data.

look_elsewhere_effect.card_en: The inflation of significance that comes from searching many places at once; the reason local and global significance differ.

trials_factor.card_en: The number of independent chances a search had to produce a fluctuation, by which local significance must be corrected.

feldman_cousins_construction.card_en: A unified way to build intervals that avoids empty and unphysical results near a boundary.

cls_method.card_en: The modified frequentist limit-setting used at colliders, which refuses to exclude models the experiment has no power to test.

type_i_error.card_en: Rejecting a true null hypothesis — a false discovery.

type_ii_error.card_en: Failing to reject a false null hypothesis — a missed effect.

jackknife_resampling.card_en: Estimating uncertainty and bias by leaving out one observation at a time.

cross_validation.card_en: Assessing a model on data it was not fitted to, by splitting the sample repeatedly.

permutation_test.card_en: Building the null distribution by shuffling labels of the data themselves.

blind_analysis.card_en: Fixing the analysis before looking at the answer, so that the result cannot be tuned towards the expected one.

binomial_distribution.card_en: The distribution of successes in a fixed number of yes-or-no trials.

exponential_distribution.card_en: The distribution of waiting times between events that happen at a constant rate; the law of radioactive decay.

log_normal_distribution.card_en: The distribution of a quantity whose logarithm is Gaussian; arises from multiplicative processes.

chi_squared_distribution.card_en: The distribution of a sum of squared Gaussian variables; the reference curve for goodness of fit.

landau_distribution.card_en: The strongly asymmetric distribution of energy loss by a charged particle in a thin absorber.

central_limit_theorem.card_en: Why the Gaussian is everywhere: sums of many independent contributions tend to it whatever their own shape.

statistical_uncertainty.card_en: Error from finite sample size, which falls as the square root of the number of events.

standard_error.card_en: The uncertainty of an estimated quantity, such as the mean, rather than the spread of the data.

pull_distribution.card_en: The distribution of residuals divided by their uncertainties; a check that the errors themselves are right.

sigma_clipping.card_en: Discarding points beyond a chosen number of standard deviations, iteratively — the common defence against outliers.

lomb_scargle_periodogram.card_en: Finding periods in unevenly sampled data, where the ordinary Fourier transform cannot be used.

autocorrelation_function.card_en: How a signal resembles itself after a delay; reveals periods and correlation times.

wavelet_analysis.card_en: Decomposing a signal in time and frequency at once, for features that come and go.

matched_filter.card_en: Correlating data with the expected shape of the signal — the optimal detector of a known waveform in Gaussian noise.

detrending.card_en: Removing a slow trend before analysing the variability that rides on it.

independent_component_analysis.card_en: Separating mixed signals into statistically independent sources.

k_means_clustering.card_en: Splitting data into groups around centres found iteratively.

boosted_decision_tree.card_en: A committee of simple trees, each fixing the errors of the last; long the standard classifier in particle physics.

random_forest.card_en: A committee of decorrelated decision trees, robust and hard to overfit.

support_vector_machine.card_en: A classifier that separates classes by the widest possible margin.

roc_curve.card_en: The trade-off between signal efficiency and background rejection as the cut is moved.

confusion_matrix.card_en: The table of what a classifier got right and wrong, class by class.

overfitting.card_en: Learning the noise of the training sample; the reason a model that fits perfectly can predict badly.

feature_importance.card_en: How much each input variable actually contributes to a trained model's decisions.

monte_carlo_simulation.card_en: Answering a problem by simulating random draws from it — from detector response to lattice field theory.

importance_sampling.card_en: Drawing from a distribution chosen to put samples where they matter, then reweighting.

rejection_sampling.card_en: Drawing from a simple distribution and keeping points that fall under the target one.

toy_monte_carlo.card_en: Repeating the whole analysis on many simulated pseudo-experiments to learn how its answer fluctuates.

information_criterion.card_en: Model comparison that trades goodness of fit against the number of parameters, as in AIC and BIC.

model_selection.card_en: Choosing between competing descriptions of the same data, by evidence, criterion or cross-validation.

si_units.card_en: The International System of Units (SI) is the modern metric system built on seven base units — metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela — from which all other units are derived; since 2019 every base unit is defined by fixing an exact value of a fundamental constant of nature.

gaussian_units.card_en: The Gaussian unit system is a centimetre-gram-second (CGS) system for electromagnetism in which the Coulomb constant equals one, so electric charge carries mechanical dimensions and factors of 4*pi*epsilon_0 disappear from formulas while factors of the speed of light appear explicitly in field equations.

planck_units.card_en: Planck units are natural units defined by setting the speed of light, the gravitational constant, the reduced Planck constant and the Boltzmann constant to one, which makes the Planck length, time, mass and temperature the characteristic scales at which quantum gravity effects become significant.

natural_units.card_en: Natural units are unit systems used in particle physics where the speed of light and the reduced Planck constant are set to one, so mass, energy and momentum share one unit (typically the electronvolt) and formulas lose their factors of c and hbar.

atomic_units.card_en: Atomic units are a system used in atomic physics and quantum chemistry where the electron mass, elementary charge, reduced Planck constant and Coulomb constant equal one, making the Bohr radius and the Hartree energy the natural scales of atomic structure.

aharonov_bohm_effect.card_en: Quantum effect in which a charged particle is affected by an electromagnetic potential even in a region where both electric and magnetic fields vanish, revealing that potentials are physically meaningful.

law_of_conservation_of_momentum.card_en: The total momentum of an isolated system stays constant: forces between its parts cancel pairwise, so nothing is gained or lost overall. A direct consequence of the homogeneity of space.
